🌍 Iran, Iraq judicial cooperation deepened across various fields: Ejei

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Judiciary Chief Gholam-Hossein Mohseni-Ejei has said cooperation between Iran and Iraq has expanded in various fields, including the legal and judicial sectors, stressing Tehran’s readiness to further strengthen ties with Baghdad.

Mohseni-Ejei made the remarks on Tuesday during a meeting with Faik Zidan, head of Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council, who was visiting Tehran at the head of a high-ranking judicial delegation.
​
He said judicial and legal relations between the two countries has developed through memorandums of understanding and agreements, adding that Iran was prepared to provide further assistance and cooperation to Iraq’s judiciary.
​
Ejei called for special judicial and legal arrangements to facilitate travel for Iranian and Iraqi pilgrims visiting holy sites in both countries throughout the year.
​
He also stressed the importance of expanding legal and judicial cooperation to help address challenges facing Iranian and Iraqi traders and businesspeople.
​
Referring to security cooperation, Ejei said the security of Iran and Iraq was closely interconnected, making it necessary for the two sides to swiftly and decisively coordinate efforts to counter any security threats along their shared border or from foreign actors.
​
Zidan, for his part, said the Iraqi government and people stood in solidarity with Iran following aggression by the United States and Israel against the country.
​
He said Iraq has not forgotten Iran’s support during difficult periods, including after 2003 and during the fight against terrorism, and condemned the United States’ “economic terrorism” against Iran.
​
Zidan also stressed the need for the full implementation of judicial agreements between Iran and Iraq, describing their cooperation as rooted in a shared understanding of the need for strategic relations.

🎙 Iranian companies join Automobility 2026 as auto parts trade with Russia rises eightfold

📌 Moscow, IRNA – The 30th edition of MIMS Automobility Saint Petersburg 2026, Russia’s international exhibition for auto parts, aftermarket products and automotive services, has opened in St. Petersburg with the participation of Iranian companies in a unified national pavilion.

Iranian Ambassador to Russia Kazem Jalali addressed the opening ceremony, attended by Russian officials and representatives from participating countries, including China and South Korea. He said Iran’s presence at the exhibition for the fifth consecutive year demonstrates the two countries’ determination to expand industrial cooperation.
​
Jalali said trade between Iranian auto-parts companies and Russia has increased eightfold over the past five years, highlighting the growing potential of both markets.
​
He added that Iran has around 1,850 companies active in auto-parts manufacturing and the automotive supply chain, with a number of knowledge-based and industrial capabilities showcased at the event.
​
The fifth Iranian national pavilion was established with authorization from the Trade Promotion Organization of Iran and cooperation from the Association of Homogeneous Propulsion and Auto Parts Industries. Seven Iranian parts and supply-chain companies, along with two trading firms, are participating across 162 square meters.
​
More than 30 Iranian industry executives and business representatives are also attending meetings with Russian manufacturers, distributors and automotive companies.
​
Held for the first time in St. Petersburg, MIMS Automobility 2026 brings together more than 1,500 companies and is expected to attract over 45,000 professional visitors. The exhibition runs through August 28 at Expoforum.
